text:
An officer can order you out of the car without suspecting you of anything.

It is settled law, and it surprises almost everyone the first time it happens. The moment goes better if you have already been through it once.

The officer can order you — and your passengers — out of the car, even with no suspicion that anyone did anything wrong.

Pennsylvania v. Mimms, 434 U.S. 106 (1977); Maryland v. Wilson, 519 U.S. 408 (1997)

Amparo has a free drill for exactly this moment — Step Out of the Car. Three minutes, no account, English or Spanish.

Practice it, then build your free glovebox pack: https://www.amparohq.com/arena/?sit=step&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=organic&utm_content=step-out_en
